items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: we had a friend there named BAILEY that owned (unintelligible) two or three places.

ctx.x: work. Roy was a guy like me, he liked to play and I always -- so we'd go after work to some of the joints around Baltimore and jam. We jammed all over Baltimore, everynight. We'd get home the next day around 12:00 o'clock half soused and sleep all day and then go to work.

So one night we were playing over to one of -- we had a friend there named BAILEY that owned (unintelligible) two or three places. And we were over there playing this night and Cab Calloway's band was playing at the Hippodome Theater. And I, that night I was standing up in a chair half juiced, playing "Memories of You" on alto. And Cab walks in and slipped and says, "what's this," you know. So he offered me a job with the band, you know. And Roy says -- so when he left, Roy said, "Man, you've got a break to go…

So I said, aw, he was drunk, he was just kidding. He don't need me." So that next day I didn't go down. I told him I'd be down but I didn't go. So Roy said, "man, you're crazy, the man wants you to come down there." So I didn't go. So the very next day I was in the hotel on Pennsylvania Avenue and Doc CHEATHAM (PHONETIC) and Walter Thomas walked in and said, man, Cab was looking for you yesterday. Why didn't you come down?" I said, "I thought he was kidding." I said, "I'll be down today."
